title: The Small Boat: private real-world scene study

story.about: A working yacht carries people through an ocean swell. This is the photographic payoff scene under development.
story.whyCare: Weight, scale and a human choosing a course make the sea feel tangible. The complete film must later earn this scene through a continuous transformation.
story.hook: A bow is already moving through living water.
story.beginning: Read the full-size vessel and its crew in a restrained parallel track.
story.development: The swell works against the immersed hull, sail and wake; a sailor turns attention to the sea.
story.tension: Will physical contact, water and crew continuity remain believable through the scene?
story.payoff: The vessel continues under sail, with people firmly aboard.
story.ending: Leave the boat moving toward open water, without an explanatory card.
story.withheld: The sailor close view until the yacht has established physical scale. This study does not claim the missing paper transformation exists.
amplify: Bow-water contact and spray returning to the sea
Continuous marine sound across picture cuts
remove: Orange canopy inconsistent with the cream-sail wide

script.action: Parallel tracking view establishes the moving navy-hulled yacht and retained crew.
script.sound: Recorded sea bed; bow-water detail only at observed contact.

script.action: The sailor turns attention toward open water, keeping her hand on the wheel and other hand on the rail. Use the early trim before orange fabric enters.
script.sound: Sea continues; restrained wood weight if justified by observed movement.

script.action: Return to the progressing sailing take; allow its motion to continue.
script.sound: Hold the same sea and let the last water movement breathe.

assets.prompt: Accept for private wide-shot use within source 0.0–2.25s only. The navy hull, cream sails and rigging retain photographic structure; the same source crew remains aboard while continuous water rolls under the immersed hull and bow spray develops. The camera creeps forward and the stern reaches the left frame boundary near the tail, so the full 3.0625s take fails the requested complete-vessel framing. It is not an approved final welcome film or close-up human identity proof.
